title: Lee Collins fails as Allen's replacement
summary: Russell brought in New Orleans trumpeter Lee Collins to replace Red Allen, but Collins was out of his depth with the tight band and Allen treated him graciously.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Well, the same thing happened at another time when Luis Russell wanted to bring in somebody to replace...

Well, he was bringing in a fellow named Lee Collins from New Orleans, a trumpet player. He wanted to replace Red Allen in the band. And this fellow, he was supposed to be the best trumpet player from New Orleans. There was a big build-up about him. And of course, Red knew
him, and they all knew one another...

Red didn't say anything, you know. So anyway, this fellow come in from New Orleans and joined Russell's band. And Russell's band at that time was real tight. I mean, Lee... Everybody knew one another and knew what was going to happen. If one of the fellows was going to make a curve(?) this way, everybody could feel it -- this-that-and-the-other, you know? And here comes Lee Collins with a big build-up from New Orleans, a young fellow, nice young man... And anyway, he started playing. He was going to take Red's place. But boy... He just wasn't capable. He just wasn't capable. He couldn't do it. And Red knew it. Red was very nice about it. He let the man play and all that. He didn't ridicule him or anything like that.

But I mean, the fella, he was over his head, for one thing; comin' to New York was another thing; and then bein' set in a band like Russell's band... I mean, we knew everything we were doing! It wasn't a band where you just come up and they stick some music in front of you. We knew everything we were playing. And the numbers we were playing were not the type that you heard other bands playing! And this fellow, he was just... He was just lost completely.
You know, he'd never heard nothin' like that before. And it was hard for him to even try to get adjusted. So he couldn't make it.

And I've got to give Red a lot of credit, too, because Red did nothing to ridicule him, and tried to help him out as much as possible, and everything else... He tried to make him feel at home. It was just that the man was scared to death, and he was just out of his class, that's all. Yeah, Red was... I was surprised to see Red was so gracious at first. But...
